submitter: bugfix_357_component_identity lane — RFC_046 PHASE 2, ROUND 2. Round 1 was REVISE, gated by bug_historian (high) on a defect that is real and is now closed with code plus a stated residual, not with an argument. THREE seats independently made the same medium objection about scope — the identity carry applied to every interactive section rather than to what adoption creates — and that is narrowed. Every other objection is answered below with the check that settles it.
rationale:
THE MINT, precisely. A tool page arrives as one `<div class="tool-page">` fragment with no `<section>`, so the section regex matches nothing and the documented fallback stores the whole fragment as ONE section named "section" — the sentinel for identity unknown. `enrichSectionsWithPlannedNames` then replaces that sentinel with `planned[Position-1]` from `pages.sections`, and `enrichSectionsWithComponentIDs` resolves the resulting NAME to a component UUID. `hero` is planned first on every affected page, so a whole interactive tool is bound to the shared hero component. [MEASURED 2026-08-23] 22 live rows, 12 of them BORN THAT DAY — this is a current rate of about a dozen a day, not history.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIXES WERE BOTH WRONG, AND WHAT SEPARATES THEM. Round 1 re-typed the row and was unsafe: Layer 2's carry-forward matches stored rows to incoming ones by `sections[i].ComponentName == p.slot` — exact slot-name equality, no fallback to position, component_id or bytes — so changing a slot name makes the match fail, control reaches the re-append arm, and the page silently GAINS a section while the tool moves (LANDMINES, this lane's own entry). Round 2 recorded and changed nothing, and was rightly called the estate's documented detect-but-never-block habit.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MAKES BOTH ACHIEVABLE: slot_name and component_id are DIFFERENT FACTS READ BY DIFFERENT CONSUMERS. `component_id` joins to `content_components` — it is what check_required_fields_missing evaluates a schema against (`check_required_fields_missing.go:80`), what regeneration renders, and what ContentDataCanFillTemplate consults. That is where 100% of this bug's damage lives. `slot_name` is the page-local positional name Layer 2 matches on, with 420 Go references as of 2026-08-23. That is where 100% of the landmine lives. So this change corrects the component and NEVER TOUCHES THE SLOT NAME OR pages.sections. The landmine is not managed, mitigated or tested around — it is never armed. `enrichSectionsWithPlannedNames` is left completely unmodified.

WHY THIS IS NOT A SIXTH INFERENCE, which is the objection RFC_046 exists to raise. Nothing is guessed. The fragment is bound to a component whose template is the identity function `{{.body}}` with the fragment as `content_data.body` — and ONLY after rendering that template and checking the output is byte-identical to the bytes being stored. The component provably produces them. `RenderTemplate` uses text/template (verified at the import), so no escaping occurs, but the check is what makes that a fact rather than an argument: edit the seeded template into something that wraps, and adoption STOPS instead of corrupting rows. The adoption is a real RenderTemplate call, so the row also earns a genuine RFC_046 provenance stamp through the resolver phase 0 just repaired — no new stamping machinery. When adoption cannot complete, `component_id` stays NULL and the row is honestly unknown, which is the state RFC_046 asks for and strictly better than a confident wrong answer. The page serves identically either way: assembly emits rendered_html regardless.

THE ESTATE HAS NO WAY TO SAY 'THESE BYTES ARE THE CONTENT', which is why one gets invented per page. [MEASURED 2026-08-23] every page_components row in the fleet holding a tool fragment is typed hero — 22 of 22, no correctly-typed exemplar anywhere — and content_components holds ZERO components whose template is a bare {{.body}} and none named adopted-fragment/passthrough/verbatim. The seed supplies that missing representation.

SCOPE (owner rulings 2026-08-02 §2 and RFC_022's narrowing, stated rather than assumed). This is new authority on a shared seam — `save_page_sections` is the single INSERT every composition path flows through — so it ships as an OPT-IN FIELD WITH THE UNSAFE DEFAULT OFF rather than as a documented contract, which is exactly what that ruling prescribes. By RFC_022's narrowing it is therefore NOT architecture-scope: opt-in, unsafe side defaults OFF, and zero live consumers name it — enumerated, not asserted: SELECT over active agent_definitions for 'adopt_unidentified_fragments' returns 0. The six live carriers of save_page_sections as of 2026-08-23 are page-build-handler, pageflow-builder, page-rebuild, page-rerender, site-work-orchestrator and tool-recreation-handler; per the 2026-07-29 ruling they are to be TOLD, not merely counted, and the guarantee that changes for them is: a fallback-adopted fragment now records a component that provably produces its bytes, or none — and carried bytes keep their own identity. ⚠ STATED BLIND SPOT: save_page_sections registers no ActionInputSpec, so this key is invisible to the RFC_022 optional-key budget check — 'not counted', which is not the same as 'under budget'.

plan.summary: Stop bugs_open/357's producer minting mislabelled rows, behind an opt-in key defaulting OFF. A fallback-adopted fragment that declares no data-component is bound to a seeded `adopted-fragment` component ({{.body}}) after a byte-identity round trip proves that component reproduces its bytes, or left honestly unidentified — never bound to its positional slot name. Layer 2's carry now restores identity ONLY for adopted-fragment rows (narrowed in round 2), so carry semantics for every other component are untouched. NO slot name is changed and pages.sections is never touched, so the carry-forward landmine is never armed.

edits.rationale: The adoption itself, plus the opt-in key both halves share. adoptFragmentSection resolves the adopted-fragment component by function, RENDERS its template with the fragment as body, and binds only if the output is byte-identical — that check is what makes this constructive fact rather than a sixth inference, and it is also the guard against anyone later editing the seeded template into something that wraps or escapes. On any failure it returns false having changed nothing, so the caller leaves the row unidentified rather than guessing. carriedIdentity is a two-line helper rather than an inline conditional because the two Layer 2 arms must agree: they are the same decision about the same bytes, and the last time they diverged nobody noticed for a day.
edits.sketch: rc := &RenderContext{ContentData: map[string]interface{}{"body": s.HTML}}; rendered, _, _, err := RenderTemplate(template, rc, logger); if rendered != s.HTML { return false }; s.ComponentID = componentID; s.ContentData["body"] = s.HTML; s.RenderedTemplateSHA = rc.RenderedTemplateSHA

edits.rationale: Mark the one place identity is INVENTED rather than carried: the no-<section> fallback that stores a whole fragment as one section. Set only when the fragment ALSO declares no data-component, i.e. when nothing about the bytes says what they are. Not persisted — it describes how the section got here, which the row has no business claiming. Marking it is what lets the binding decline without having to re-derive 'was this invented?' from the name, which would be another inference.
edits.sketch: FallbackAdopted: componentName == "section"   // inside the existing fallback append

edits.rationale: The behaviour change, at the one seam where a positional NAME becomes a claim about what the bytes ARE. When armed and the section is fallback-adopted with no data-component: adopt, or leave unidentified — and in both cases `continue`, so a failed adoption can never fall through into the name resolution and become a successful guess. A self-declaring fragment is left alone entirely: the attribute is evidence about the bytes, which RFC_046 §4 keeps precisely because it is evidence rather than position. enrichSectionsWithPlannedNames is NOT touched — the slot name still comes from the plan, because that is what slot names are for and it is the key Layer 2 matches on.
edits.sketch: if adoptFragments && sections[i].FallbackAdopted { if dataComponentRe.FindStringSubmatch(sections[i].HTML) == nil { if adoptFragmentSection(ctx, db, &sections[i], logger) { continue }; continue } }

edits.symbol: SavePageSectionsAction — Layer 2 carry arms (preload + splice + re-append)
edits.rationale: NARROWED IN ROUND 2, and the objection was right. The first version carried the stored identity for EVERY interactive section, which is far broader than the diagnosed bug: a legitimately-typed component that a plan intended to swap would have been silently kept at its OLD identity. I defended that as 'a fix rather than a regression' — by argument, not measurement, which is the move this gate exists to catch, and three seats caught it. The preload now also reads the stored component's FUNCTION and carriedIdentity returns nothing unless it is 'adopted-fragment'. That still delivers the causal fix — adoption must survive a rebuild or the next one re-mints the plan's identity over an adopted row — and changes carry semantics for nothing else. The MATCH remains slot-name equality, untouched.
edits.sketch: LEFT JOIN content_components cc ON cc.id = pc.component_id ... if id := carriedIdentity(carryStoredIdentity, p.componentID, p.componentFunction); id != "" { sections[matchedIdx].ComponentID = id }  // carriedIdentity returns "" unless storedComponentFunction == adoptedFragmentFunction

edits.rationale: The missing representation, seeded idempotently so a re-run cannot mint a second identity and split the fleet's adopted rows. HELD deliberately: content_components is a shared library that LoadComponentLibraryAction enumerates, so a row that exists is a row something can offer to a planner. component_level='fragment' and category='internal' make that structurally unlikely against callers that filter on either, and the residual (a caller passing component_level='all' with no category filter) is stated in the file rather than hidden. Nothing needs it before arming, and with the flag ON but the seed absent adoption degrades to the honest unknown. input_schema declares body with NO source, which is tolerated by design (bareSourceValues in component_source_guard.go), so neither the birth gate nor CLC-025's daily check — whose baseline is frozen at 2026-08-22 and would go RED on a new offending field — has anything to say about it. Verify block uses DO/RAISE, not SELECT, because a non-empty result set cannot stop a COMMIT.
edits.sketch: INSERT INTO content_components (...) SELECT 'Adopted Fragment', ..., '{{.body}}', 'adopted-fragment', ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM content_components WHERE function='adopted-fragment'); DO $$ ... RAISE EXCEPTION ... $$;

edits.rationale: Refuses rather than cascades. Once armed, live page_components rows carry this component's id, and deleting it would orphan them — a row pointing at a deleted component cannot be re-rendered at all, which is WORSE than the state bugs_open/357 describes, where a row at least names a component that exists. The refusal names the correct order instead: disarm, re-type the bound rows, then remove.
edits.sketch: IF bound > 0 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'refusing to remove adopted-fragment: % rows are bound to it', bound; END IF;

edits.rationale: Built as PAIRS, because the interesting assertion is a refusal and a refusal only means something if what was refused was genuinely available. The armed case asserts the fragment binds the adopted component, keeps its slot name UNCHANGED, gains content_data.body and earns a stamp, and registers no hero lookup — so if the name path ran at all sqlmock fails it. Its sibling runs the identical fixture DISARMED and asserts it binds hero, which is simultaneously the decoy control and the default-OFF proof. Plus: a wrapping template is refused and changes nothing; an unseeded estate leaves the row unidentified rather than falling back to the guess (a real state, since the seed is held); and a self-declaring fragment is left to its attribute. MUTATION PROVEN: disabling the adoption branch fails the armed test on all four assertions.
edits.sketch: enrichSectionsWithComponentIDs(ctx, db, sections, logger, true) ... if s.ComponentName != "hero" { t.Errorf("renaming the slot is what arms the landmine") }

edits.symbol: layer2PreloadWithIdentity + the spliced test's HTML bind
edits.rationale: The preload fixture widens to the query's new column set, and — the part that matters — the spliced test's rendered_html bind is pinned to the TOOL bytes instead of AnyArg. Found while making this change: a fixture row one column short makes rows.Scan fail, the Layer 2 loop logs and skips, and THE SPLICE NEVER RUNS, at which point the provenance assertions pass while testing nothing. Only the re-append case noticed, because it asserts a row COUNT that a skipped splice cannot satisfy. Pinning the bytes makes a skipped splice fail every case, and that vacuity mutation is proven to fail it.
edits.sketch: mock.ExpectExec("INSERT INTO page_components").WithArgs(pageID, 1, layer2ToolHTML, "hero", AnyArg, AnyArg, AnyArg, nil)

grounded_in: architecture_review/RFC_046 — owner RULED option 1 on 2026-08-22 (stamp identity at the point of production), and authorised repairing the mislabelled rows in principle only AFTER the stamp is live and readable. Phase 0 made the stamp actually reach the database today; this is the round that stops new rows needing repair.

LIVE MEASUREMENT 2026-08-23: the bug file's population query returns 22 rows, 12 created 2026-08-23. All position=1, slot_name='hero', component=hero, no data-component in the HTML. pages.sections on an affected page reads ["hero","generic-text-block"] with rebuild_policy='generic' — the plan really does put hero first and these pages really are rebuilt automatically.

LIVE MEASUREMENT 2026-08-23: every page_components row in the fleet whose HTML contains a tool fragment is typed hero — 22 of 22, so there is no correctly-typed exemplar to copy. And content_components contains ZERO components whose template is a bare {{.body}}, and none named adopted-fragment/passthrough/verbatim — the representation this seeds does not exist today.

LANDMINES.md — 'CORRECTING a page_components.slot_name makes the NEXT rebuild append the tool beside a freshly generated section': Layer 2 matches on sections[i].ComponentName == p.slot, exact string equality, no fallback. This plan changes no slot name and does not touch pages.sections or the matcher, so the landmine is never armed; a pinning test asserts rows written == incoming count.

check_required_fields_missing.go:80 joins content_components ON cc.id = pc.component_id and reads cc.input_schema — so the false 'missing headline' findings (9 sitting in needs_human_review as of 2026-08-23) are produced by the component axis, and correcting that axis fixes them at the root with no change to the checker.

component_library.go imports text/template, not html/template — so a {{.body}} template reproduces stored markup verbatim rather than escaping it. The adoption does not rely on this: it renders and compares bytes.

component_source_guard.go bareSourceValues includes the empty string, so the seeded body field declaring no source is tolerated by both the birth gate and CLC-025's daily at-rest audit, whose baseline is frozen at 2026-08-22 and would otherwise go RED on a new offending field.

Owner ruling 2026-08-02 §2 (new authority on a shared seam ships as an opt-in field, unsafe default OFF) and RFC_022's 2026-08-11 narrowing (such a field is not architecture-scope when the unsafe side defaults OFF and zero live consumers name it — enumerated: 0 active agent_definitions mention adopt_unidentified_fragments).

ROUND 1 GATING OBJECTION, ANSWERED AT THE SOURCE: bug_historian cited bugs_closed/039 ('a section naming a missing component renders an empty stub') against risk #5's new NULL-component population, and was right that round 1 asserted 'the page serves identically either way' without verifying it on the RERENDER path. Read at source this round: resolveComponent (rerender_page_sections_action.go:377) falls through to the slot-NAME map when component_id is empty, so an unadopted row named 'hero' resolves to hero there and the fresh-render entry re-emits hero's id. That is a REAL residual and it is now stated in the code, the bug file and this submission rather than glossed: phase 2 REDUCES the mint, it does not eliminate it for the rare adoption-failure case. What is newly pinned is the half at the seam being changed — TestAdopt_UnidentifiedRowStillWritesItsBytes asserts an unidentified section still reaches the INSERT with its bytes intact and a NULL component bind, so it is not dropped, blanked or skipped (039's shape).

prior_art_librarian asked for the live-DB claims to be re-verified rather than quoted. Re-run 2026-08-23: content_components rows whose btrim(html_template) = '{{.body}}' = 0, and rows with function/name matching adopted-fragment/passthrough/verbatim = 0 — the seed is non-duplicative. Layer 2's match is `sections[i].ComponentName == p.slot` read at save_page_sections_action.go (the switch above the splice), not taken from the LANDMINES entry. LoadComponentLibraryAction's filters are at load_component_library_actions.go:145-172 (component_level, category, is_active), which is what makes the seeded row structurally unlikely to be offered — and the residual (a caller passing component_level='all' with no category filter) is stated in the migration file itself.
plan.risks:
1. THE FLAG GOVERNS TWO BEHAVIOURS, NOT ONE. Adoption and the Layer 2 identity carry share a key because neither is useful alone — adoption that does not survive a rebuild is not a fix. The cost is that arming turns on both at once. Stated rather than split, because splitting them would create a combination (adopt without carry) whose only effect is to re-mint the mislabelling on the next rebuild.

2. RESOLVED IN ROUND 2: the identity carry is now restricted to adopted-fragment rows, so no legitimately-typed component's carry semantics change at all. The broader version is not deferred, it is withdrawn — if 'carried bytes keep their identity' is right in general it deserves its own round with its own measurement of how many sections would flip, which is what the guardian seat actually asked for.

3. WHAT ARMING WOULD LOOK LIKE IF IT WERE WRONG, named in advance: a page whose row count goes UP by one after a rebuild (the landmine firing through some path this plan believes untouched — invisible to any check that only asks whether the tool is still present, which is why the count is the assertion); a tool page whose rendered_html stops containing class="tool-page" or its <script>; or an adopted row whose component_version_id is NULL, meaning the round trip did not earn a stamp and the binding is weaker than claimed.

4. THE SEED IS HELD, so 'armed but not seeded' is a reachable state. It degrades to the honest unknown and there is a test for exactly that. The reverse — seeded but not armed — is inert: nothing looks the component up.

5. UNIDENTIFIED ROWS ARE A NEW POPULATION. A fragment that cannot be adopted gets component_id NULL where today it would get a (wrong) component. That is the state RFC_046 asks for, but NULL component_id has its own consumers — bugs_open/039's stub guard and the componentless-pages check among them — and on the evidence here the case should be rare (the seeded template is the identity function, so the round trip fails only if someone edits it). It is worth watching after arming rather than assuming.

6. NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: the 22 existing rows. The owner authorised that repair in principle only after the stamp is live and readable, which needs the next roll; it is written and HELD as a separate migration. And no detector for the five OTHER page_components writers — real value, separate lane, named so it is not mistaken for covered.

7. THE RERENDER PATH STILL RE-DERIVES IDENTITY BY NAME, and this is the honest limit of this round. resolveComponent falls through to the slot-name map when component_id is empty, so a row that FAILS adoption is re-bound to hero by the next rerender. Adoption fails only if the seeded identity template has been edited, so the population should be near-zero, but 'should be' is not 'is': the correct fix is the same cut applied to the rerender producer, and it is named here and in the bug file as follow-up rather than smuggled into this round.

8. GOVERNANCE GAP, now tracked rather than merely disclosed: save_page_sections registers no ActionInputSpec, so this key is invisible to the RFC_022 optional-key budget check. Adding a spec for an action with this many existing config keys is its own change with its own blast radius and does not belong in a bug fix; it is filed as follow-up so the gap is counted rather than permanent.

9. SectionData.FallbackAdopted is in-memory only. Checked this round rather than assumed: SectionData carries no struct tags and is never marshalled — it is built and consumed inside one action invocation. If a future consumer round-trips it through JSON the flag degrades to false, which fails SAFE (no adoption, today's behaviour).

10. DEPLOY VERIFICATION, named explicitly at the debug_historian seat's request: after the roll, probe the RUNNING pod for the capability rather than trusting the image tag or a green CI — grep the binary for adoptFragmentSection's own literals with BOTH a must-be-present and a must-be-absent control, because a probe with no negative control returns the same answer on every service.
